title: How can I create different visual styles for the same 2D game assets?
author: MeliodasKaplan
selftext:
Hey,

I’m a playable ads developer.

I already have finished playable projects where everything works (gameplay, layout, logic). Now I’m trying to create **visual variations of the same project** by only changing the assets.

What I want is:

* Keep the same layout and gameplay exactly the same
* Keep all objects in the same size and position
* Only change the visual style (different themes / looks)

But the problem is, most tools I’ve tried are creating completly new assets not variations of originals.

I’m wondering if there’s a good workflow or tools for this kind of “asset swap but same structure” process.

Any advice would be appreciated 🙏

comments.author: Own-Rub-2091
comments.body: I've been fully enjoying pixellab.ai. thay allow you to use reference images. There's much to learn for me still but you might give it a try

replies.author: MeliodasKaplan
replies.body: Thanks, I took a look at it with the credits it gives for initial registration. I think I can do the job I want, and if I can figure out how to use Asperite a bit more, maybe I can even do more than I want. I'll probably sign up and do some testing this month.

replies.author: Own-Rub-2091
replies.body: Im not much an artist so its been a life saver for me. They got me for the 12 a month and i feel its worth it. I dont use Asprite though. It's free to use their browser pixel lab and it does the same thing for the most part.

comments.author: AutomaticTalent
comments.body: I had Claude build a swappable audio/grafix (AGX) set for my game to do exactly what you are wanting to do.  It's not (yet) plug and play but it does give the basic structure for the assets and flow so that building new sets is easier.
